subject: environmental-science
title: Soil Horizons and Profiles
welcome_lead: From leaf litter to bedrock — read the layered story under your boots.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on soil horizons, texture and pH.
final_note: A spadeful of soil holds more microbes than there are humans on Earth.

concepts.def: Topsoil; mixed mineral and organic matter; site of most biological activity.
Subsoil; accumulation of leached clays, iron and aluminium oxides.
Weathered parent material; less biological activity.
Sand-silt-clay classification (USDA); determines drainage and fertility.

walkthroughs.body_html: A typical mid-latitude soil shows distinct horizons reflecting bioclimatic processes.
Sand drains well but holds few nutrients; clay holds water and cations but compacts. Loams balance both.
Most crops favour pH 6–7. Below 5, Al³⁺ becomes toxic; above 8, P availability drops.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.
Forest fires alone.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
